fresh.title: Stress adaptation and hypersensitivity in 5-HT neuronal systems after repeated foot shock.

fresh.title: Brain region-specific action of ketamine as a rapid antidepressant.
fresh.scope_assessment: Eligible for brain-system extraction: experiments establish region-specific neural responses to ketamine and test local activity and LHb NMDAR dependence. Regional electrophysiology and interregional timing are central. Molecular targets and behavioral outcomes are relevant here as mechanistic qualifiers rather than isolated human clinical efficacy claims.
fresh.design_and_roles: Male adult C57BL/6 and NR1-floxed mice, with chronic restraint stress (CRS) or naive comparison conditions. Systemic racemic ketamine was 10 mg/kg intraperitoneally. The study combines in vivo tetrode recording and photometry with ex vivo slice recordings after systemic exposure, plus separate direct slice perfusion experiments (10 micromolar or 1 millimolar ketamine). Chemogenetic CNO/hM3D activation, optogenetic eNpHR inhibition, and local NR1 knockout are mechanistic interventions. Cell/unit counts and animal counts differ: baseline tetrodes include 239 LHb units in 15 mice and 147 CA1 units in 10 mice, not 386 mice. Per-panel samples vary; there is no single whole-study denominator.

central_facts.statement: Systemic ketamine suppressed LHb NMDAR synaptic currents in depressive-like mice while CA1 pyramidal currents were not significantly suppressed; naive mice lacked the LHb suppression.
central_facts.source_quote: In the present study, using in vitro slice electrophysiology, we found that a single systemic injection of ketamine in depressive-like mice, but not naïve mice, specifically blocked NMDAR currents in LHb neurons, but not in hippocampal CA1 neurons.
central_facts.qualifications: C005 and C007 distinguish region and depression state. At 1.5 mA LHb NMDAR currents were 49.4±11.8 versus 12.7±2.7 pA (saline versus ketamine, p=.002); AMPAR currents and surface NR1 did not significantly change after ketamine. Slices were prepared one hour after systemic exposure, not an exclusively in vivo current assay.

fresh.title: Psilocybin-assisted neurofeedback for the improvement of executive functions: a randomized semi-naturalistic-lab feasibility study.
fresh.scope_assessment: Eligible for cognitive/behavioral extraction: randomized feasibility evaluation compares a package of psilocybin microdosing plus frontal-midline theta neurofeedback with a passive control, reporting objective executive tasks and self-rated functioning. The package comparison cannot isolate psilocybin or neurofeedback effects.
fresh.design_and_roles: 37 adults were randomized (18 experimental, 19 passive control). Three dose-adjustment sessions preceded three neurofeedback sessions over a three-week schedule. Mean 1.14 g is fresh Psilocybe mexicana truffle mass, not pure psilocybin. Objective task denominators after exclusions are 31 reference-back, 35 switching and 33 stop-signal; the conflict-monitoring task was excluded because 12/37 performed below threshold. All 37 contributed self-reports; individual goal groups overlap and have their own counts (cognition 17, presence 18, mood 13, connection 5). Control participants had not yet begun microdosing during the evaluated comparison.

central_facts.statement: The intervention did not demonstrate improvements in objective working-memory updating, set shifting or response inhibition relative to passive control.
central_facts.source_quote: Regarding the transfer of psilocybin-assisted NF to EFs, we found notable effects on self-reported daily life EFs with a high effect size. However, there were no discernible effects observed in experimental objective tasks.
central_facts.qualifications: C024 reports null group effects for reference-back and switching and no between-group SSRT change (p=.334). Two significant effects were not specific executive-function benefits: a reference-back condition effect and stop-task go-trial RT change. Conflict monitoring was excluded, so it cannot be called an observed null.

central_facts.statement: The experimental group reported greater improvement than passive control in everyday working memory, shifting, monitoring and inhibition; self-rated working memory moved into the normal range.

fresh.title: Ketamine sensitization: Influence of dose, environment, social isolation and treatment interval.
fresh.scope_assessment: Safety scope includes abuse-liability evidence. Locomotor sensitization is explicitly studied as an animal proxy relevant to addiction; no diagnosed addiction, self-administration, human incidence or neurotoxicity measured.

central_facts.statement: Repeated ketamine produced sensitization at 5, 10 and 20 mg/kg, with the lower-dose evidence in fine movements; robust ambulation sensitization was clearest at 20 mg/kg.
central_facts.source_quote: Although 20 mg/kg was the only dose that showed a significant increase in locomotion on Day 1, there was evidence of sensitization at all three doses.
central_facts.qualifications: Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats, IP daily five days; n7 per ketamine dose, n3 saline. Ambulations increased versus day1 on days3–5 at20; fine-movement increases were dose/day dependent at all three doses. This is an animal behavioral proxy relevant to abuse liability, not demonstrated addiction.

central_facts.qualification: Mephedrone half-maximum at 1.5–2 h and near baseline at 2–3 h; MDMA onset ~0.75 h, peak 1–1.5 h, near baseline at 4 h. These are effect times, not plasma Tmax or half-life.

fresh.title: Psychedelic use and psychological flexibility: The role of meaningful intention and decentering
fresh.scope_assessment: Eligible for subjective experience: the study relates retrospective psychedelic phenomenology to self-reported psychological flexibility. Correlations and adjusted null findings are central; this is not a demonstrated drug-induced improvement or a performance-based cognitive task.
fresh.design_and_roles: Cross-sectional online survey of prior classic psychedelic users. 449 attempted, 267 were eligible after cleaning, and the source explicitly gives 114 for regression after missing-data handling. Correlations use pairwise sample sizes. Respondents considered their sole or most meaningful prior experience. LSD and psilocybin were most common, with other classic psychedelics pooled. The Cognitive Flexibility Inventory is a self-report measure. Ego-dissolution totals span 0–800, not the single-item 0–100 scale.

central_facts.statement: Respondents described mystical experience, ego dissolution, external connection, and psychological insight during their selected prior psychedelic experience.
central_facts.source_quote: Most participants generally agreed to having a mystical experience, a loss of sense of self (i.e., identity), disrupted ego-boundaries, and greater external connection during their only or most meaningful psychedelic experience.
central_facts.qualifications: Descriptive retrospective reports in a selected sample; not incidence in all psychedelic users or change from baseline. The same section describes new insight into life goals and circumstances.
